blocks.t: Stokes’ Theorem for Surfaces with Holes

Stokes’ Theorem holds for an oriented surface S that has one or more holes (Figure 16.67). The surface integral over S of the normal component of ∇* F equals the sum of the line integrals around all the boundary curves of the tangential component of F, where the curves are to be traced in the direction induced by the orientation of S. For such surfaces the theorem is unchanged, but C is considered as a union of simple closed curves.

In Section 16.3, we found that a field F being conservative in an open region D in space is equivalent to the integral of F around every closed loop in D being zero. This, in turn, is equivalent in simply connected open regions to saying that ∇* F = 0 (which gives a test for determining if F is conservative for such regions).
